prior_importants.description: The new `.replace(/\.+$/, '')` runs on each PATH match. A match with a long run of dots that is not at its end takes quadratic time. One `a/<65,530 dots>x` in an area field costs about 2.1e9 start-and-backtrack steps of V8 irregexp time on the event loop. PATH itself handles this input in linear time, so the cost comes only from this delta.

`HEADING` runs on every line outside a fence. Its lazy capture is followed by `\s*#*\s*$`, so a single line like `# a` + N spaces + `b` costs about N³/6 backtracking steps and blocks the event loop of whatever process runs intake.

PLACEHOLDER only matches the bare token, so in a terse field a placeholder with a trailing period or Markdown wrapping passes as filled: Affected area `TBD.`, Suspected area `Unknown.`, Source PR `N/A.` or Time box `` `n/a` `` are reported complete, while the same text without the period is flagged vague.

EMPTY_LIST_ITEM is tested with the `m` flag across the whole field, code fences included, so any pasted unified diff that adds or removes a blank line (a line that is just `+` or `-`) marks a fully filled Reproduction, Expected against actual, Findings, Scenarios or Proof field as vague.

A path-like glob such as `src/**/*.ts` or `src/**` in `Files in scope` (the form asks for "One path or glob per line") becomes the single module `**` and matches no ADR glob, so a repo-wide refactor fires neither trigger.

Follow-up has no `area` field, so its whole body feeds the triggers. The scope globs and paths used as inputs in `Scenarios` then fire adr-area or module-boundary falsely. `Findings`, which the form defines as "the file and line it points at", is the real area field.

When the area names a file by its GitHub permalink, the extracted path starts with `github.com/<owner>/<repo>/blob/<ref>/`. That path matches no ADR glob and no module, so `adr-area` and `module-boundary` don't fire and the design gate passes when it should fail.

findings.description: The adr-area check only asks whether a ticket path lies inside an ADR glob, never whether the ADR area lies inside the ticket's path. A directory or single-star glob that covers an ADR-governed file or subdirectory fires nothing, so a chore or bug skips the design that decision 176 requires.
findings.body:
**adr-area only checks one direction of containment**

```ts
const inAdrArea = (path: string): boolean =>
  adrAreas.some((area) => area.test(path) || area.test(`${path}/`));
```

This catches a ticket path inside an ADR area (`src/cli/ls.ts` against `src/cli/**`). It misses the reverse: a ticket area that *contains* an ADR area. [Decision 176](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/f1b1927eb2968f4d80e2dabc6fd8397876be97ea/docs/adr/0176-a-ticket-has-a-type-and-only-some-types-need.md) forces a design on any type that "**touches** an ADR area", and the `IntakeContext.adrAreas` JSDoc says the same. The forms ask for this kind of broad area:
- `chore-refactor.yml` Files in scope: *"One path or glob per line. Nothing outside these may change."* That field is an upper bound, so any ADR-governed file inside it can be edited.
- Bug Suspected area: *"the file, module or command suspected"*, so a module-level answer like `src/claude/` is expected.

**Triggers** (with ADR globs narrower than a module, which the existing test's `src/cli/*.ts` already uses):
- refactor, Files in scope `src/claude/*.ts`, adrAreas `['src/claude/hooks.ts']`. `^src/claude/hooks\.ts$` does not match the literal `src/claude/*.ts`, so the result is `triggers: []`, `needsDesign: false`.
- bug, Suspected area `src/claude/`, adrAreas `['src/claude/hooks/**']`. PATH yields `src/claude`, and neither `src/claude` nor `src/claude/` matches `^src/claude/hooks/.*$`, so the result is `needsDesign: false`.

Either ticket skips design review even though its scope covers an ADR area. This partly overlaps the owed `src/**/*.ts` finding: that finding's adr-area half has the same root cause. This case is wider, though, because a plain directory with no wildcard misses too. The fix below handles both.

**Fix:** also fire when an ADR glob's static prefix (the text before its first wildcard) lies under the ticket path's static prefix, comparing at a `/` boundary. It errs toward firing, which suits a gate whose job is to force a design.

<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/f1b1927eb2968f4d80e2dabc6fd8397876be97ea/src/core/ticket-intake.utils.ts#L175-L179>

process_issues.description: Round 4 importants-only budget: only correctness, security (the untrusted issue body is input handling) and guards ran. conventions, docs, simplicity, context and maintainability were skipped by the round budget. spec was skipped because there is no closing issue or --spec source, and workflow-safety because no workflow changed. The consolidator was not spawned because the reviewers returned a single finding in total.

The validator confirmed the finding but could not see the suggestion text. The orchestrator then rewrote the suggestion to keep the existing line-175 WHY comment and checked it against the validator's four conditions: it spans 175-179 and re-emits lines 178-179, it uses context.adrAreas for the raw globs, it compares prefixes at a '/' boundary, and it keeps the forward check.
The guards reviewer did not open .claude/project.env (FILE_NAMING_ROLE_DIRS) or read ADR 0176 in full. It relied on the merge gate's passing test and lint run for file layout.
